Explore the codebase and the Next.js version-specific docs in node_modules/next/dist/docs/ to understand:
1. What framework conventions exist for data loading / routing.
2. Whether there is a pattern for prefetching only partial data (e.g., a project title) when navigating from a dashboard to a project page, without prefetching the rest of the project page.
3. Where the dashboard and project pages/routes are located in the codebase.

Return a concise summary with file paths and the relevant Next.js documentation file/section that supports the approach.

## Summary ### Codebase structure - Next.js version: `16.4.0-canary.24` (Cache Components / App Router). - Dashboard (projects list): `/workspace/app/page.tsx` - Renders `{project.name}` - Project detail route: `/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` - Uses `PageProps<'/projects/[slug]'>`, `Suspense`, and `await params`. - Calls `getProjectTitle(slug)` and `getProjectDetails(slug)`. - Data layer: `/workspace/lib/data.ts` - `getProjectTitle(slug)` — cached (`'use cache'`), fast lookup. - `getProjectDetails(slug)` — cached (`'use cache'`), but intentionally delayed 800 ms. - Layout / metadata: `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` - Next.js config: `/workspace/next.config.ts` - Only `cacheComponents: true` enabled; `partialPrefetching` is **not** enabled yet. ### Framework conventions for data loading / routing - **File-system routing**: routes map to files under `app/` (`page.tsx` = route, folders = segments). - **Server Components by default**: data fetching happens in async React Server Components. - **Cache Components**: enabled via `cacheComponents: true`. Use `'use cache'` to cache async functions/components. - **Streaming with Suspense**: slow or dynamic data should be wrapped in `` with a fallback. - **Dynamic data**: reads of `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()` should be inside a `` boundary so they don’t block the App Shell. Key docs: - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/03-layouts-and-pages.md` — file-system routing, pages, layouts. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/04-linking-and-navigating.md` — prefetching, streaming, client-side transitions. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/06-fetching-data.md` — Server Component data fetching and Suspense. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/01-getting-started/08-caching.md` — Cache Components and `use cache`. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/cacheComponents.md` ### Pattern for prefetching only partial data The supported mechanism is **Partial Prefetching** + **per-link prefetching** with `prefetch={true}`. How it maps to this project: 1. Enable Partial Prefetching globally: ```ts const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, partialPrefetching: true, } ``` 2. Restructure `/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` so that the **title** (fast/cached) is resolved at the App Shell / per-link prefetch level, while the **details** (slow) stream in behind ``. 3. Use `` from the dashboard. This tells Next.js to resolve URL-specific cached data (`params`/slug) before navigation. 4. The slow `getProjectDetails` should be inside a `` boundary so it is **not** part of the prefetch; it streams after navigation. Key docs: - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/prefetching.md` — App Shell vs full prefetch. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/optimizing-prefetching.md` — resolving URL data at prefetch time with `prefetch={true}`, excluding content from prefetches. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/02-guides/adopting-partial-prefetching.md` — migration guide, moving URL data behind Suspense. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/partialPrefetching.md` — global flag. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/02-route-segment-config/prefetch.md` — per-route `prefetch = 'partial'`. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/02-components/link.md` — `` semantics. - `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/navigation.md` and `/workspace/node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/prefetch.md` — `unstable_navigation()` and `unstable_prefetch()` for finer control over what is deferred. ### Current issue in the project `/workspace/app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx` currently awaits both `getProjectTitle` and `getProjectDetails` together with `Promise.all`, and the whole component is wrapped in a single ``. Under Partial Prefetching, reading `params` inside the `Project` child is correct (it keeps URL data behind Suspense), but `getProjectTitle` is cached and cheap while `getProjectDetails` is slow. To prefetch only the title, split them: - Keep `

{title}

` outside the details `` (or in its own cheap Suspense) so it can resolve during the per-link prefetch. - Move `

{details.description}

` and the activity list into a separate child wrapped in `` so it streams after navigation and is not prefetched. Then set `prefetch={true}` on the dashboard links and enable `partialPrefetching: true`. ### Build verification Running `npm run build` confirms: - `/` is static. - `/projects/[slug]` is already Partial Prerender (`◐`) because `params` is read inside Suspense and `cacheComponents` is enabled. Adding `partialPrefetching: true` and splitting the title/details will make the dashboard link prefetch only the title portion. session_id: ses_f77ac53adffezQ8ey4NzPybV1O

events.content:
Implemented partial prefetching so the project title resolves during the dashboard link prefetch while the details stream after navigation.

Changes made:
- `next.config.ts`: enabled `partialPrefetching: true` alongside `cacheComponents`.
- `app/page.tsx`: set `prefetch={true}` on dashboard project links.
- `app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`: split the title into a separate `Suspense` boundary so it can be prefetched; wrapped heavy details in another `Suspense` that streams post-navigation.

Build passes and confirms `/projects/[slug]` is Partial Prerender (`◐`).
